# AI Hook Generator for Reels: 36 Hooks That Make the First Three Seconds Clear

You press play on your Reel, hear the first sentence back, and realize it could introduce almost anyone’s video. The swipe happens before the point arrives.

![Three Hook Lab hooks for one video](https://uploads.postiz.com/8cLEoX1RU8.png)

An AI hook generator for Reels is most useful when it gives you specific opening options—not a vague instruction to “be more engaging.” The examples below show how to turn one video idea into spoken lines, on-screen text, and a clear angle you can test.

## Fitness and wellness

1. **Contrarian:** “Stop trying to work out for an hour.”  
   **On-screen text:** “20 minutes counts”

2. **Mistake:** “This is why your healthy routine disappears by Wednesday.”  
   **On-screen text:** “The Wednesday problem”

3. **Question:** “What if your low energy is coming from your morning routine?”  
   **On-screen text:** “Check this first”

4. **Before/after:** “I changed one part of my walk and it stopped feeling like a chore.”  
   **On-screen text:** “Make walks easier”

5. **Specific audience:** “If you work at a desk all day, try this before you stretch.”  
   **On-screen text:** “For desk workers”

6. **List promise:** “Three gym habits beginners can skip this week.”  
   **On-screen text:** “Skip these 3”

## Food and cooking

7. **Problem:** “Your meal prep is taking too long because you start in the wrong order.”  
   **On-screen text:** “The prep-order fix”

8. **Reveal:** “The ingredient that makes this [ADD: dish] taste finished.”  
   **On-screen text:** “Don’t skip this”

9. **Constraint:** “I made dinner with what was already in the freezer.”  
   **On-screen text:** “Freezer dinner”

10. **Question:** “Why does your homemade sauce taste flat?”  
    **On-screen text:** “One quick check”

11. **Challenge:** “Can a [ADD: budget] grocery haul cover [ADD: number] dinners?”  
    **On-screen text:** “Budget dinner test”

12. **Unexpected method:** “I stopped measuring this ingredient, and the recipe got easier.”  
    **On-screen text:** “Cook by this cue”

## Beauty and style

13. **Mistake:** “This is the makeup step that keeps making your base look heavier.”  
    **On-screen text:** “Why it looks cakey”

14. **Specific audience:** “If your outfits feel unfinished, start with this—not a new purchase.”  
    **On-screen text:** “Finish the outfit”

15. **Comparison:** “Same [ADD: item], two ways: which one would you actually wear?”  
    **On-screen text:** “Look 1 or look 2?”

16. **Confession:** “I was using this skincare product at the wrong point in my routine.”  
    **On-screen text:** “Wrong order”

17. **Fast result:** “Here’s how I make a basic outfit look intentional in two steps.”  
    **On-screen text:** “2-step outfit fix”

18. **Question:** “What should you check before buying another neutral?”  
    **On-screen text:** “Check this first”

## Business and freelance work

19. **Hard truth:** “Your client is not ignoring your proposal because it is too short.”  
    **On-screen text:** “It’s this instead”

20. **Process:** “Here is the first line I write before I build a proposal.”  
    **On-screen text:** “Start here”

21. **Mistake:** “If every content idea sounds like a pitch, this is probably why.”  
    **On-screen text:** “Fix the angle”

22. **Question:** “What would change if your offer answered one problem, not five?”  
    **On-screen text:** “One problem first”

23. **Template:** “Use this sentence when a client asks, ‘What exactly do you do?’”  
    **On-screen text:** “Try this answer”

24. **Behind the scenes:** “I turned one customer question into [ADD: number] content ideas.”  
    **On-screen text:** “From question to posts”

## Creator education

25. **Pattern interrupt:** “Your Reel does not need a longer intro. It needs this decision.”  
    **On-screen text:** “Choose the angle”

26. **Question:** “Would a stranger know who this video is for in three seconds?”  
    **On-screen text:** “The 3-second test”

27. **Mistake:** “The hook is not your video title read out loud.”  
    **On-screen text:** “Different jobs”

28. **Demonstration:** “Watch what happens when I replace one generic opening.”  
    **On-screen text:** “Before → after”

29. **Specific audience:** “For creators who keep rewriting the first sentence: use this framework.”  
    **On-screen text:** “Stop rewriting”

30. **Test setup:** “I wrote three openings for the same idea. Here is what each one is trying to do.”  
    **On-screen text:** “3 angles, 1 topic”

## Home, travel, and everyday life

31. **Reveal:** “The reason this small room feels crowded is not the furniture.”  
    **On-screen text:** “It’s the layout”

32. **Local guide:** “Skip the obvious stop if you only have [ADD: number] hours here.”  
    **On-screen text:** “Limited-time route”

33. **Problem:** “Packing for [ADD: number] days got easier when I stopped choosing outfits first.”  
    **On-screen text:** “Pack this way”

34. **Before/after:** “This one reset made my kitchen easier to use every morning.”  
    **On-screen text:** “Small kitchen reset”

35. **Question:** “What do you actually need for a weekend trip?”  
    **On-screen text:** “Pack less”

36. **Challenge:** “Can this corner become useful without buying anything new?”  
    **On-screen text:** “Use what you have”

## How to choose a hook for your Reel

Pick the hook that matches the job of the video. A **question** works when viewers recognize the problem immediately. A **mistake** works when you can name a common wrong move and show the correction. A **contrarian** opening works when you can support a surprising position in the next few seconds. A **specific-audience** hook works when the viewer needs to know, fast, that the video is meant for them.

Do not choose the cleverest line in isolation. Choose the one your next shot can prove. If the spoken hook says “three mistakes,” show the first mistake right away. If it promises a comparison, put both options on screen. The opening and the video need to make the same promise.

## A simple way to test your opening

Write three hooks for one topic, each using a different angle: one question, one mistake, and one contrarian claim. Keep the body of the Reel as similar as practical. Then review the recordings alongside the first frame and on-screen text.

Ask four practical questions:

- Can someone understand the topic with the sound off?
- Does the first visual support the spoken line?
- Does the next beat answer the hook instead of restarting the introduction?
- Can you deliver the line naturally in the first three seconds?

If a hook needs a long explanation before the value appears, narrow it. “How to improve your content” is broad. “The first sentence that makes this tutorial sound generic” gives the viewer a concrete reason to stay.

## FAQ

### What should an AI hook generator for Reels create?

Useful output gives you more than a single sentence: several angles, the spoken line, matching on-screen text, and a direction for the next beats of the video. That lets you select an opening that fits your topic and audience.

### Should every Reel start with a controversial statement?

No. Contrarian hooks are one option. A clear question, a recognizable mistake, a visual demonstration, or a direct audience callout can be a better match when the claim needs nuance.

### How many hooks should I test?

Start with three distinct angles for the same topic. The purpose is not to generate endless variations; it is to find a promise you can clearly fulfill in the Reel.

### Can I use these hooks for Instagram Reels and TikTok?

Yes. Adapt the wording to your voice, show the evidence quickly, and make sure the first frame supports what you say.

## What the tool returns

Here is a published example of the input and the shortened output:

**You send:** "Hooks for a 30s TikTok about why most people quit the gym in January — energetic, for beginners."

**You get back (shortened):**
- **Positioning:** "The gym isn't the problem — your first week is." You own the beginner-who-keeps-quitting angle.
- **Hooks (5+, each with spoken line + on-screen text + type):**
  1. *Contrarian* — 🗣 "Stop going to the gym every day." / 🖥 "Day 1 is where you quit"
  2. *Question* — 🗣 "Why does everyone quit by January 20th?" / 🖥 "The January 20th wall"
  3. *Mistake* — 🗣 "You're not lazy. You're doing week one wrong." / 🖥 "Week 1 mistake"
- **Recommended pick:** #3, with one line on why it fits a beginner audience.
- **Script:** 0–3s hook · 3–10s the mistake · 10–22s the fix in 3 steps · 22–30s CTA.
- **Caption:** short caption + CTA + hashtags, plus one filming tip.
